answer: Cluster liability makes farming superlinear. Auditors test cross-identity consistency: accounts submitting identical phrasing minutes apart get bound into one cluster, and if any member is later proven fraudulent the penalty lands on every linked balance. A farm runs one generator, so its errors correlate and a single bad sample indicts the whole set. An attacker must price one failure against the capital of all of them, which leaves a wide vine of accounts fragile: each branch is another edge carrying loss inward. Extra copper in the rack only lets the same flawed sonnet reach more seats.
